_about: Every sample is a public artefact with a pinned SHA-256. Nothing here is redistributed:
the APKs are fetched by scripts/fetch_corpus.py from the project that publishes them,
and the hash is verified before the file is used. `.gitignore` keeps *.apk out of git,
so this file is the corpus, not the binaries.
The `note` field is the label's basis and is mandatory: the benchmark harness refuses a
sample without one, because a guess multiplied by a corpus size becomes a precision
figure. Read the notes carefully - `vulnerable` means 'a documented weakness exists in
this app', NOT 'this build can detect a weakness in this app'. Several of these are
expected to be missed, and that is the point of measuring.

samples.name: insecurebankv2
samples.label: vulnerable
samples.note: InsecureBankv2 (Dinesh Shetty): a deliberately vulnerable banking app published for security training, with documented access-control, exported-component and insecure-storage weaknesses. Basis: the app's own documentation states it is intentionally vulnerable. Label means documented weakness, not detectable-by-this-build.

samples.name: mastg-uncrackable-1
samples.label: vulnerable
samples.note: OWASP MASTG crackme level 1: hides a secret string in the app and checks for root. Basis: published by OWASP MASTG as an intentionally crackable training target. Its weakness is in-code secret storage and anti-tampering - neither is modelled by this build, so a miss is expected and is a true finding about our coverage.

samples.name: mastg-uncrackable-2
samples.label: vulnerable
samples.note: OWASP MASTG crackme level 2: as level 1 plus native-code validation. Basis: published by OWASP MASTG as an intentionally crackable training target. Weakness is in-code secret storage and native checks; not modelled here.

samples.name: mastg-uncrackable-3
samples.label: vulnerable
samples.note: OWASP MASTG crackme level 3: as level 2 with additional anti-debugging. Basis: published by OWASP MASTG as an intentionally crackable training target. Weakness is anti-analysis and in-code secret storage; not modelled here.

samples.name: androguard-test-debug
samples.label: benign
samples.note: Tiny test APK shipped in androguard's test suite, built to exercise the parser: one activity, no permissions, no network. Basis: it exists only as a parser fixture, and nothing documents a weakness. This is 'no known vulnerability', not an audit.

samples.name: androguard-testactivity
samples.label: benign
samples.note: Larger androguard test application used to exercise activity and intent parsing. Basis: parser fixture from androguard's suite; no documented weakness. 'No known vulnerability', not an audit.

samples.name: a2dp-volume
samples.label: benign
samples.note: Real third-party utility app (a2dp volume control) used by androguard as a parser fixture for a non-trivial manifest. Basis: no CVE or documented weakness found for this release; the app ships with a launcher and standard components. This is a weak basis and is labelled as such - a real audit could flip it, and if it does, the corpus should be corrected rather than the result explained away.
